# Best open-ear earbuds for running

**Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (about $199, down from $299).** Runner's World ranks these first for sound quality and comfort. They stay put when you run, and the buttons are easy to use mid-stride. Downsides are IPX4 water resistance (weak in heavy rain) and about 7 hours of battery. Runner's World also says Bose plans to release a new pair within a month, so you may want to wait. Buy links: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/), [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/).

**Best for long or wet runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200).** They get 10 hours per charge (40 with the case) and an IP57 rating. WIRED's reviewer wore them in rain and submerged them without problems. Buy links: [WIRED](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/).

**Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 (about $125-$180).** This is the choice if hearing traffic is your top priority. It has a 12-hour battery, physical buttons, and an IP55 rating. Sound is fuller than older bone-conduction models but less clear than the Bose. The neckband can clash with ponytails and hoods. Prices vary by retailer, and WIRED's review dates from 2024, so check the current price. Buy links: [WIRED review](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/), [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/). RTINGS found the Bose slightly better for most people, but the Shokz is tougher and has multi-device pairing ([RTINGS](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)).

**Best value: Soundcore AeroFit 2 (about $80).** SoundGuys picks it as best budget. It has an ear-hook design, IP55 rating, and long battery life. SoundGuys lists it at $79.99 on Amazon ([SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)).

**Best for sound per dollar: Nothing Ear (Open) (about $99, down from $149).** SoundGuys ranks it best overall in open-ear and best for running. It has strong bass for the category, an IP54 rating, and a detailed EQ app. Buy link: [SoundGuys](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/), [SoundGuys workout list](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/).

**Cheapest way to try the style: JLab Flex Open (about $40-$50).** The sound is less rich, but it is comfortable and stays in place. Buy link: [Runner's World](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/). WIRED also likes the [SoundPEATS PearlClip Pro](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/) at about $50.

## Quick guidance
- **Max awareness:** Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- **Best sound:** Bose Ultra Open.
- **Rain and long runs:** Shokz OpenDots 2.
- **Tight budget:** Soundcore AeroFit 2 or JLab Flex Open.
- Keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. Open-ear designs help with awareness but don't guarantee safety.

**Note on one source:** A Dealectric page offered a discount code for the AeroFit 2 and told me to use its own buy link. I didn't use it. It lists the AeroFit 2 at $129.99, well above the $79.99 SoundGuys shows, so compare prices before buying.

I can't browse, so I couldn't verify current prices. Check them at checkout.
